title: Per-route priority rebalancer and forecasted invoice breakdown PRD
creator: Aisha Kapoor
summary: Deliver a per-route priority rebalancer that automatically shifts burst credits across call-groups and surfaces a forecasted invoice breakdown to customers and invoices. This will reduce surprise overage charges, improve fairness across routes, and enable self-serve remediation for mid-month spikes.
background: Customers have reported sudden unexpected overage charges when one route in a multi-route integration spikes (e.g., embeddings-heavy batch jobs) and exhausts shared burst credits. Current billing shows only end-of-cycle totals, which offers no actionable signal. Previous PM work (see PM-31415 and PM-31112) covers entitlement inheritance and soft-cap policies but lacks per-route rebalancing and forecasted invoice visibility.
problem_statement: When tenant-level burst credits are consumed by a single noisy route, other critical routes experience degraded throughput or unexpected overage invoicing. Teams must manually monitor and redistribute credits (or open support tickets) mid-cycle. We need an automated, auditable mechanism to rebalance credits, plus proactive invoice forecasts so customers can act before overage invoices are generated.
goals: 1) Reduce customers experiencing >25% unplanned overage by 50% within first 3 months after rollout. 2) Provide a per-route forecast card in Console showing projected invoice delta with >90% accuracy for top 5 routes. 3) Enable self-serve rebalancing and one-click reserve allocation in Console.
non_goals: Changing core quota accounting, replacing billing backend, or introducing new hard limits for existing plans. This feature should augment existing entitlements/soft-cap logic, not replace invoicing engine.
user_stories: As a platform engineer, I want burst credits to be automatically redistributed from low-priority routes to high-priority routes during surge windows so that SLAs are preserved.
As a finance lead, I want a forecasted invoice breakdown by route so I can budget and review before final invoice generation.
As a developer, I want a one-click temporary reserve that pins X credits to a route for Y hours so my critical endpoint doesn't starve during batch jobs.
As a customer success manager, I want an audit trail of rebalancer actions to justify invoice adjustments when opening support tickets.
requirements: Functional: Implement a rebalancer service that runs hourly and applies a priority-weighted decay algorithm to redistribute up to configurable percentage (default 20%) of tenant burst credits across routes.
Functional: Rebalancer must respect per-route and per-caller entitlements and never move credits that are explicitly pinned via reserve API.
Functional: Expose an API endpoint /v1/billing/forecast?tenant_id=<>&horizon_days=7 that returns per-route projection and estimated invoice delta (JSON schema documented in Confluence).
UX: Console panel 'Invoice Forecast' that shows top 10 routes, current consumption, projected consumption, projected invoice delta, and a CTA to 'Reserve Credits' or 'Increase Tier'.
Observability: Emit structured events for each rebalancer decision (reason, credits_moved, source_route, dest_route, timestamp, user_override) to telemetry pipeline (metrics + logs).
Security/Compliance: All operations must be auditable; store rebalancer decisions in audit log with immutable identifiers.
Operational: Provide a kill-switch and dry-run mode to verify the model before applying in production.
Policy: If rebalancer cannot reconcile due to KMS errors or missing entitlements, it must surface an alert to billing-ops Slack channel and not attempt silent movement.
api_contract_examples: Example: GET /v1/billing/forecast?tenant_id=rdw-1234&horizon_days=14 -> returns [{route: 'embeddings/import', projected_tokens: '1.2M', projected_invoice_delta_cents: '23900', confidence_pct: '92'}]. PATCH /v1/entitlements/rdw-1234/reserve -> {route: 'chat/sync', credits: 5000, duration_hours: 72} returns reserve_id and expires_at.
acceptance_criteria: Automation: Rebalancer successfully runs in dry-run mode against a staging tenant and generates a decision log; product signoff obtained.
Accuracy: Forecast API achieves >=90% accuracy for top 5 routes over 7-day horizon in internal benchmark (error measured as absolute percent error against simulated usage traces).
Console: 'Invoice Forecast' UI renders without P0 visual defects, shows route-level breakdown, and the Reserve Credits flow completes end-to-end (UI -> API -> audit log).
Safety: Rebalancer respects pinned reserves and per-route hard entitlements; verified via unit tests and integration test fixture.
Observability: All rebalancer actions emit events to telemetry with schema compliance; billing-ops alert triggers on simulated KMS failure.
Docs: Update billing docs with API contract, Console UX screenshots, and an operator runbook for rollback.
success_metrics: % of customers with unplanned overage reduced (target: 50% reduction among initial cohort)
Number of self-serve reserves created (target: 200 in first 30 days for pilot customers)
Mean time to detect and remediate a noisy-route incident (target: decrease by 40%)
scope_changes_and_notes: During initial scoping we debated adding per-caller time-decay credits; decided to defer and limit to tenant-level rebalancing plus per-route reserves. PM/Eng agreed this reduces complexity for billing reconciliation. Engineering requested breaking the feature into two waves: Wave 1 (rebalancer + forecast API + console view) and Wave 2 (auto-reserve heuristics + cross-tenant pooling).
rollout_plan: Phase A (internal pilot): enable for 12 sandbox tenants, monitor telemetry for 2 weeks. Phase B (opt-in customers): enable via feature flag for top 50 customers who opt in; collect feedback. Phase C (general availability): on by default for plans that include burst credits. Rollout owners: Miguel (Eng), Priya Rao (SRE), Linda Park (Billing).
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Incorrect forecasts could generate bad customer decisions. Mitigation: conservative confidence bands and explicit disclaimers; lock forecasted invoice from being used as final billing until invoice run. Risk: Rebalancer may move credits away from routes used by regulatory flows. Mitigation: introduce 'protected' label that blocks movement and surface in audit logs.
open_questions: Should per-route forecasts include model-level cost multipliers (e.g., L96 vs L10) or only token counts?
What SLA do we commit for forecast API latency (500ms target?)
How should refunds be handled if rebalancer decisions are later deemed incorrect by billing dispute?
review_feedback: Design review 2025-02-24: Add clear explanation of confidence intervals and add affordance to 'simulate' reserve before committing. Legal: confirm audit retention window for rebalancer logs. Finance: request CSV export for forecasted invoices. Engineering: requested smaller alpha for initial default redistribution (reduced to 20%).
